config.title: useMediaQuery

intro.title: useMediaQuery
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React component that changes its text and background color based on the screen width. You will learn how to use the useMediaQuery hook to detect and respond to changes in the user's viewport. The main technologies involved are React, TypeScript, and the window.matchMedia API. This will help you create responsive designs that adapt to different device sizes.
intro.usecase: The useMediaQuery hook is essential for creating responsive interfaces that adapt to different screen sizes and device capabilities. Developers use it to conditionally render components like navigation menus (switching between hamburger menus and full navigation bars), adjust dashboard layouts (rearranging cards and charts on tablets vs. desktops), and toggle dark/light modes based on system preferences. This pattern appears in virtually every modern web application—from e-commerce sites that optimize product grids for mobile to admin panels that show/hide sidebar panels based on available space. Implementing media queries programmatically allows developers to build more dynamic, accessible user experiences that respond to the user's environment in real time.

objectives: Implement a custom useMediaQuery hook that returns a boolean based on a media query string.
Initialize the hook's state with the current match status of the provided media query.
Construct an event listener to update the state when the media query match changes.
Configure the hook to add and remove the event listener using useEffect.
Apply the useMediaQuery hook within a component to conditionally render UI elements.
Manipulate component styling or content based on the boolean value returned by the hook.
Integrate the useMediaQuery hook to control responsive behavior in a React application.

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The imports are added at the top of the file, enabling React and state management functionality.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close, but make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'. Check your import statement syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. You need to import React and useState from 'react' to proceed.

steps.title: Create the useMediaQuery custom hook
steps.instruction: Create a custom hook function named useMediaQuery that takes a query parameter of type string.
steps.hint: Define a function that accepts a string parameter and returns a boolean value. You can start with a simple implementation that returns false for now.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create your useMediaQuery hook here
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named useMediaQuery that accepts a string parameter and returns a boolean value.
successCriteria: The useMediaQuery function is defined with a query parameter of type string and returns a boolean.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your function is named exactly 'useMediaQuery' and accepts a string parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've created a function named 'useMediaQuery' with a string parameter. The function should return a boolean value.

steps.title: Initialize state for media query match
steps.instruction: Inside your useMediaQuery hook, call useState with false as the initial value and destructure the returned array to get matches and setMatches variables.
steps.hint: Use const [matches, setMatches] = useState(false); to create state that tracks whether the media query matches.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useMediaQuery hook will have a matches state variable initialized to false and a setMatches function to update it.
successCriteria: The useMediaQuery hook contains a useState call with false as initial value, and matches and setMatches are properly destructured.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling useState with false and destructuring both matches and setMatches from the returned array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The hook should initialize state using useState(false) and destructure matches and setMatches from it. Try adding: const [matches, setMatches] = useState(false); inside the hook.

steps.title: Create the media query listener handler
steps.instruction: Inside your useMediaQuery hook, define a function named handleChange that takes a MediaQueryListEvent parameter and calls setMatches with e.matches.
steps.hint: The function should update the matches state based on the media query event's matches property.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your useMediaQuery hook will have a handleChange function that updates state when media query events occur.
successCriteria: The handleChange function is defined with a MediaQueryListEvent parameter and calls setMatches with e.matches.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it takes a MediaQueryListEvent parameter and calls setMatches with e.matches.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleChange function should be defined inside useMediaQuery with proper parameter typing and state update logic.

steps.title: Set up the media query match and listener in useEffect
steps.instruction: Add a useEffect hook inside your useMediaQuery function that creates a MediaQueryList object, sets the initial matches state, adds the change listener, and returns a cleanup function to remove the listener.
steps.hint: Use useEffect to run side effects. Inside it, create a MediaQueryList with window.matchMedia(), set the initial matches state, add your handleChange as a listener, and return a cleanup function that removes the listener.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useEffect hook is added to the useMediaQuery function with proper setup and cleanup for the media query listener.
successCriteria: useEffect is added to the useMediaQuery function, creates a MediaQueryList object, sets initial matches state, adds the handleChange listener, and returns a cleanup function that removes the listener.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added useEffect, but make sure it creates the MediaQueryList, sets initial matches, adds the listener, and returns a cleanup function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The useEffect hook is missing or incomplete. Review the hint and try again.

steps.title: Return the matches value from the hook
steps.instruction: At the end of your useMediaQuery function, return the matches state variable.
steps.hint: The hook should return the current value of matches so components using it can access the media query status.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useMediaQuery hook now returns the matches state, making it usable by components.
successCriteria: The useMediaQuery function returns the matches state variable.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're returning the matches variable from the hook function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The hook should return the matches state variable at the end of the function.

steps.title: Create the main App component
steps.instruction: Create a function component named App that returns a JSX element. The component should be empty for now, returning a simple wrapper like a <div>.
steps.hint: Define a function called App that returns JSX. You can start with a basic <div> as the return value.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have an App component that returns a JSX element, ready to use the custom hook in later steps.
successCriteria: The App component is defined as a function that returns JSX, such as a <div>.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've made progress, but ensure you've defined a function named App that returns JSX (e.g., a <div>).
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component is not defined correctly. Make sure to create a function called App that returns a JSX element like a <div>.

steps.title: Use the custom hook in the App component
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, call the useMediaQuery hook with the media query string '(max-width: 768px)' and store the returned value in a variable named isMobile.
steps.hint: Call the hook like you would call any other React hook, passing the media query string as an argument.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will have a variable isMobile that holds the boolean result of the media query check.
successCriteria: The useMediaQuery hook is called with the string '(max-width: 768px)' and the result is stored in a variable named isMobile.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling useMediaQuery with the exact string '(max-width: 768px)' and storing the result in a variable named isMobile.
steps.feedbackWrong: The hook call or variable assignment is missing or incorrect. Check that you're calling useMediaQuery with the media query string and storing the result.

steps.title: Add conditional rendering based on media query
steps.instruction: In the App component's JSX, add conditional rendering that shows 'Mobile view' when matches is true and 'Desktop view' when false.
steps.hint: Use a ternary operator to conditionally render different text based on the matches value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will display 'Mobile view' when the screen width is 768px or less, and 'Desktop view' otherwise.
successCriteria: The App component's JSX contains a ternary operator that conditionally renders 'Mobile view' or 'Desktop view' based on the matches value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using the matches value in a ternary operator to show the correct text for each condition.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check your conditional rendering syntax. You need to use a ternary operator with the matches value to display different text.

steps.title: Export the App component
steps.instruction: Export the App component as the default export so it can be rendered by React.
steps.hint: Use the 'export default' syntax followed by the component name.
steps.analogousExample:
// Export a component as default
export default App;
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is exported as the default export, making it available for rendering.
successCriteria: The App component is exported as default using 'export default App;'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using 'export default App;' to export the component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component is not exported as default. Use 'export default App;' to make it available for rendering.
